revision_note: Regenerated to align task_ids with sop_modules.json. All task_ids now match SOP character-for-character. Rate values preserved from v0.1.0 where task intent matches.

MODIFIER_STACKING_ANALYSIS.description: Aluminum siding repaint has a stacking PARTITION: chalk_severity modifier (FAC_ALRP_CHALK) applies to PREP tasks only. QT modifier (FAC_ALRP_QT) applies to coating tasks only. Access and environmental modifiers apply to all variable-rate tasks. Two independent stacking pools.
MODIFIER_STACKING_ANALYSIS.worst_case_prep: heavy chalk (1.75) x scaffold (1.60) = 2.80x on prep tasks
MODIFIER_STACKING_ANALYSIS.worst_case_coating: QT3 (1.00) x scaffold (1.60) x full_sun (1.15) x cold_temp (1.30) = 2.39x on coating tasks
MODIFIER_STACKING_ANALYSIS.worst_case_theoretical_prep: heavy chalk (1.75) x scaffold (1.60) x moderate_wind (1.25) = 3.50x (theoretical extreme — wind affects outdoor tasks)
MODIFIER_STACKING_ANALYSIS.worst_case_theoretical_coating: QT3 (1.00) x scaffold (1.60) x full_sun (1.15) x cold_temp (1.30) x moderate_wind (1.25) = 2.99x (meteorologically improbable)
MODIFIER_STACKING_ANALYSIS.resolution: Both pools well under 4.0x cap. Stacking partition keeps prep and coating modifier pools separate — chalk severity never inflates coating rates.

prep_tasks.note: FAC_ALRP_CHALK applies to prep/wash tasks ONLY. FAC_ALRP_QT does NOT apply to prep tasks.

coating_tasks.formula: effective_rate = base_rate / (FAC_ALRP_QT x FAC_EXT_ACCESS x FAC_EXT_WIND x FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE x FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP)
coating_tasks.max_stack: 1.00 x 1.60 x 1.25 x 1.15 x 1.30 = 2.99x (QT3 baseline — QT2 at 0.85 actually speeds up)
coating_tasks.note: FAC_ALRP_CHALK does NOT apply to coating tasks. Environmental modifiers apply to coating tasks only.

fixed_tasks.note: Administrative gates, equipment setup/cleanup, chalk verification, DFT verification are fixed-time tasks. No modifiers applied.

siding_surface_input_group.description: Rate per SF applies to net siding field area from PaintScope. Engine divides SF by rate to calculate hours.

task_production_rates.name: Crew Mobilization & Equipment Staging
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mobilize crew, transport materials and equipment to site. Stage self-etching primer, epoxy intermediate (if coastal), finish paint, spray equipment, DFT gauge, abrasive pads, and protection materials. Verify material against spec — confirm self-etching primer (phosphoric acid + zinc), NOT STIX. ~45 min includes dual-tip setup for spray (fine-atomization 311-413 for primer + standard 413-515 for finish).

defect_tolerance.QT2: All materials on-site and verified, equipment functional
defect_tolerance.QT3: All materials on-site and verified against spec, DFT gauge present, both tip sets tested

task_production_rates.name: Scaffold / Lift Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Erect scaffold, position aerial lift, or stage extension ladders per access plan. OSHA-compliant setup with fall protection. ~90 min for typical two-story scaffold setup. Scaffold preferred for multi-story aluminum to improve spray stability for DFT control.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Level, plumb, tied off, fall protection in place
defect_tolerance.QT3: Level, plumb, tied off, fall protection in place, base plates on firm footing

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy plastic sheeting and tarps over adjacent landscape beds and plantings. Stake and secure. ~18 sec per SF. Additional concern: chalk-laden wash runoff stains landscape — protection before wash step.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Major plantings covered, gaps tolerable at perimeter
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of all adjacent landscape with secured edges

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Protection (Walkway + Patio + Driveway)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths and plastic on walkways, patios, and driveways adjacent to working elevations. ~14 sec per SF. Chalk-laden wash runoff stains concrete — drop cloths at foundation line critical.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Drop cloths covering primary traffic paths and adjacent hardscape
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full hardscape coverage with taped edges, foundation line protected

task_production_rates.name: Window Spray Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Paper or masking film over window glass + tape around frame. ~7.5 min per window. Spray method requires full glass masking.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Glass covered, minor tape gaps at corners tolerable
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full glass coverage with clean tape lines at all edges

task_production_rates.name: Door Spray Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Full cover door with masking film or plastic. ~12 min per door. Doors are larger than windows.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Door fully covered
defect_tolerance.QT3: Door fully covered with clean sealed edges

task_production_rates.name: Corner Trim Masking at Siding-to-Trim Transition
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape line or paper mask at siding-to-trim junction when trim is different color. ~1 min per LF.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Tape line applied along trim edge
defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean tape line with paper backing where needed

task_production_rates.name: Light Fixture Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Bag and tape light fixtures. ~4 min per fixture.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Fixture bagged
defect_tolerance.QT3: Fixture bagged with sealed tape edges

task_production_rates.name: HVAC Unit Cover
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Wrap condenser unit in plastic sheeting and tape. ~10 min per unit.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Unit covered with plastic
defect_tolerance.QT3: Unit fully wrapped with taped seams

task_production_rates.name: Utility Panel Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask electrical panel, gas meter, hose bibs. ~5 min per unit.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Panel covered
defect_tolerance.QT3: Panel fully masked with sealed edges

task_production_rates.name: Mix Alkaline Cleaning Solution
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mix TSP or dedicated aluminum siding cleaner concentrate with water per manufacturer directions. Load into pressure washer downstream injector. ~10 min. Increase concentration for heavy chalk projects.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Solution mixed at standard concentration, loaded into equipment
defect_tolerance.QT3: Solution mixed per manufacturer spec, concentration adjusted for chalk severity

task_production_rates.name: Pressure Wash Aluminum Siding — Standard
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pressure wash 1000-1500 PSI with alkaline cleaner (TSP) in downward spray pattern. Removes dirt, mildew, surface contamination. 750 SF/hr for chalk_severity=none. Mandatory first production step. Do not exceed 2000 PSI to avoid denting thin-gauge panels.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Visible dirt and mildew removed
defect_tolerance.QT3: All dirt, mildew fully removed. Surface clean for chalk verification.

task_production_rates.name: Pressure Wash — Light Chalk Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pressure wash with TSP at increased concentration for light chalk removal. Apply cleaner, 5-10 min dwell time, rinse at 1000-1500 PSI. Focus south/west facades. Effective rate derived from base 750 SF/hr / light chalk modifier 1.25 = ~600 SF/hr.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Visible chalk removed, light residue acceptable if verification passes
defect_tolerance.QT3: All chalk removed, chalk verification test passes with zero transfer

task_production_rates.name: Pressure Wash — Heavy Chalk Removal (Multi-Pass)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Extended wash protocol for heavy chalk. Multiple passes with TSP at increased concentration. First pass: apply cleaner, 10-15 min dwell, pressure rinse. Second pass: mechanical scrubbing on stubborn areas. Third pass: final rinse. Effective rate derived from base 750 SF/hr / heavy chalk modifier 1.75 = ~430 SF/hr.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Chalk removed after multi-pass, verification passes
defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete chalk removal, verification passes on all tested areas, documented in QC log

task_production_rates.name: Chalk Verification Gate
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: MANDATORY GATE. Hand-rub test with dark cloth on each elevation section after wash and dry. Any white chalk transfer = re-wash required. ~15-20 min per section. Must pass before scuff/prime proceeds. Applies to ALL substrate states including SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Dark cloth shows no visible chalk transfer
defect_tolerance.QT3: Dark cloth shows zero chalk transfer on all tested areas, documented in QC log

task_production_rates.name: Oxide Layer Scuff — 180-320 Grit

QT2.notes: Scuff visible oxide and high-gloss areas. Focus on elevation faces with most weathering.

QT3.notes: Full-surface scuff on all elevations. Uniform matte appearance after scuffing. No glossy areas remaining.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mechanically break Al2O3 oxide film with synthetic steel wool or 180-320 grit abrasive pads. More aggressive than vinyl light scuff. ~14 sec per SF at QT3. CRITICAL: Do NOT use real steel wool — ferrous particles cause galvanic corrosion. TIMING: must prime within 4-8 hours (2-4 hours coastal).

defect_tolerance.QT2: Scuff marks visible across majority of field, some light areas acceptable
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform scuff pattern across all surfaces, no un-scuffed glossy areas, 100% coverage verified

task_production_rates.name: Post-Scuff Dust Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Compressed air or tack cloth to remove scuff dust and abrasive residue from aluminum surface before priming. ~6 sec per SF. Self-etching primer acid must contact clean metal — dust acts as bond-breaker.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Visible dust removed from field surfaces
defect_tolerance.QT3: All dust removed, tack cloth shows clean on final pass

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Joint Assessment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Inspect siding-to-trim joints for failed caulk. ~18 sec per LF to probe and mark. QT3 only. Aluminum has minimal thermal movement at joints — less caulk failure than vinyl.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All joints inspected and failed sections marked for replacement

task_production_rates.name: Spot Caulk Replacement
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove failed caulk, clean joint, apply siliconized acrylic caulk, tool smooth. ~48 sec per LF. QT3 only. Siliconized acrylic adequate — aluminum has minimal thermal movement (polyurethane not required).

defect_tolerance.QT3: Smooth, continuous caulk bead, no gaps, no smears on adjacent surfaces

task_production_rates.name: Self-Etching Primer — Spray
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray self-etching primer (phosphoric acid + zinc) on scuffed aluminum. MANDATORY single coat. Fine-atomization tip (311-413). Single-pass technique — do NOT double-back. DFT 0.5-1.0 mil ONLY. Over-application causes cohesive failure. ~8.5 sec per SF. Midpoint 425 SF/hr.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full coverage, no bare aluminum visible, no runs or pooling
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full even coverage, no runs, no sags, uniform thin film build verified by DFT gauge spot checks

task_production_rates.name: Self-Etching Primer — Brush/Roll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush edges, roll field with 3/8 nap roller for self-etching primer. DFT control is harder with roller — risk of over-application in lap overlaps. ~29 sec per SF. Spray is strongly preferred. Brush/roll only when spray is not feasible.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full coverage, no bare aluminum visible
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full even coverage, thin film maintained, no pooling at lap overlaps

task_production_rates.name: DFT Verification — Self-Etching Primer
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: CRITICAL QC GATE. Verify self-etching primer DFT is within 0.5-1.0 mil range using wet/dry film thickness gauge. Check minimum 3 points per elevation section. Over-application (>1.0 mil) causes cohesive failure — requires strip and re-prime. ~10-15 min per zone. Unique to aluminum siding.

defect_tolerance.QT2: DFT readings within 0.5-1.0 mil on spot checks (2+ per elevation)
defect_tolerance.QT3: DFT readings within 0.5-1.0 mil on systematic grid checks (3+ per elevation), documented in QC log

task_production_rates.name: Epoxy Intermediate Coat — Spray (Coastal Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: COASTAL CONDITIONAL. Airless spray epoxy intermediate coat over cured self-etching primer. Creates corrosion barrier for salt-air environments. Standard spray tip (413-515). Single coat per manufacturer DFT spec. ~9.6 sec per SF. Midpoint 375 SF/hr.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full coverage, no bare primer visible, uniform film
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full even coverage, uniform DFT, no runs or sags, edges feathered at trim transitions

task_production_rates.name: Epoxy Intermediate Coat — Brush/Roll (Coastal Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: COASTAL CONDITIONAL. Brush edges, roll field with epoxy intermediate. Two-component epoxy is thicker and has shorter pot life — significantly slower than spray. ~36 sec per SF. Brush/roll only when spray is not feasible.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full coverage over self-etching primer
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full even coverage, smooth roller finish, no holidays

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray

QT2.notes: Economy pace — even coverage, no detailed transition work

QT3.notes: Standard pace — uniform mil build, clean transitions at J-channels

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray 100% acrylic latex finish on primed aluminum. Standard tip (413-515). No backbrush (non-porous metal). ~8 sec per SF at QT3.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Uniform color coverage, minor overspray at transitions tolerable
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform color, no runs, no sags, clean transitions at J-channels and trim

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush/Roll

QT3.notes: Standard pace — no brush marks in roller field, maintain wet edge

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush edges, roll field with 3/8 nap roller for finish coat. Smooth aluminum surface. ~30 sec per SF at QT3.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Uniform color, minor roller stipple acceptable
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform color, smooth lay-off, no roller lines or holidays

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray

QT3.notes: Same rate as coat 1 spray. Critical for full hide, proper DFT, and maximum durability.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second and final finish coat by spray. QT3 only — QT2 uses single finish coat. ~8 sec per SF. Allow recoat time per TDS between coats. No backbrushing.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform color with full hide, no runs, no sags, clean transitions

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush/Roll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second and final finish coat by brush and roller. QT3 only. ~30 sec per SF.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform color with full hide, smooth lay-off, no roller lines

task_production_rates.name: Brush Detail — J-Channels & Under-Sill
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply finish coat into J-channels, under-sill channels, and starter strip recesses. Spray may not fully penetrate these recessed areas. Estimate at 5-10% of total field SF as detail SF. ~24 sec per SF. QT3 only — primary labor differentiator between tiers.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage in all channel recesses, no bare aluminum visible, clean transitions

task_production_rates.name: Brush Cut-In at Trim Transitions
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush cut-in where siding meets corner trim, window casing, door casing, and soffit junction. Clean color line at siding-to-trim boundary. ~36 sec per LF. QT3 only.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Sharp color line at trim boundary, no bleed onto trim surface, consistent line at 6 ft viewing

task_production_rates.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walk all elevations and inspect completed siding finish for defects, holidays, coverage, and appearance. Check DFT readings from primer phase documentation. ~1.4 sec per SF average.

defect_tolerance.QT2: No obvious misses or runs visible from 10 feet
defect_tolerance.QT3: No defects visible from 6 feet, clean transitions at all trim junctions, DFT log reviewed

task_production_rates.name: Final Touch-Up
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during final walkthrough inspection. ~1 sec per SF equivalent (most area needs no touch-up).

defect_tolerance.QT2: Obvious defects corrected
defect_tolerance.QT3: All noted defects corrected, repairs blended, J-channels uniform

task_production_rates.name: Remove All Protection Materials
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all tarps, plastic, masking tape, fixture bags, window/door masks. Faster than setup — pull and fold. ~9 sec per SF equivalent.

defect_tolerance.QT2: All protection materials removed from site
defect_tolerance.QT3: All protection materials removed, no tape residue on surfaces, landscape inspected

task_production_rates.name: Scaffold / Lift Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Dismantle scaffold, return aerial lift, or stage ladders for removal. ~60 min typical teardown (faster than setup). OSHA-compliant disassembly.

defect_tolerance.QT2: All access equipment removed
defect_tolerance.QT3: All access equipment removed, no damage to landscaping or hardscape from equipment

task_production_rates.name: Clean Spray Equipment & Tools
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Flush airless sprayer, clean spray tips and filters, clean brushes and rollers. CRITICAL: flush thoroughly between self-etching primer and finish coat — primer chemistry is incompatible with acrylic finish if cross-contaminated. ~30 min average (35 min spray, 15 min brush/roll, blended).

defect_tolerance.QT2: Equipment flushed and stored
defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment flushed, tips cleaned individually and stored separately, no cross-contamination

task_production_rates.name: Final Site Cleanup & Demobilization
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Collect debris (abrasive pads, masking waste, empty containers), dispose properly, final site walkthrough, rinse hardscape if alkaline cleaner residue remains. ~20 min. No RRP waste — aluminum factory enamel is not lead-based.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Site clear of materials and debris
defect_tolerance.QT3: Site clear of materials and debris, no overspray on adjacent surfaces, client walkthrough

factor_modifiers.name: Quality Tier Rate Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Quality tier affects care and rigor on coating and detail tasks. QT2 economy = less care, faster pace. QT3 standard = baseline. Does NOT apply to prep tasks (chalk severity handles prep variation).
factor_modifiers.notes: QT2 at 0.85x = slightly faster (less care, economy-grade work). QT3 at 1.00x = baseline standard. No QT4/QT5 — aluminum is not a fine-finish substrate.

factor_modifiers.name: Chalk Severity Rate Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Chalk severity affects prep and wash task labor time. PREP TASKS ONLY — does not apply to coating, detail, or cleanup tasks. Note: chalk_severity is now dispatched to separate wash tasks (WASH_PRESSURE, WASH_CHALK_LIGHT, WASH_CHALK_HEAVY) so this modifier applies primarily to scuff and dust cleanup tasks.
factor_modifiers.notes: UNIQUE to aluminum siding repaint. Chalk severity drives PREP LABOR TIME. Heavy chalk (1.75x) reflects more aggressive scuffing of chalk-softened oxide, and extended dust cleanup. Wash tasks are now separate by chalk_severity so the modifier applies to scuff/dust tasks that are shared across all chalk levels.

factor_modifiers.name: Access Type Height Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Access type drives production rate reduction for elevated work. Shared across all exterior specs.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applied per elevation. Protection setup/teardown, equipment setup/cleanup, chalk verification, DFT verification, and fixed administrative tasks are NOT affected. Scaffold preferred for multi-story aluminum to improve DFT consistency.

factor_modifiers.name: Wind Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Wind condition modifier for spray operations. High wind is a STOP condition.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applies to spray tasks only. High wind (>15 mph) is a STOP. CRITICAL for self-etching primer: wind during thin-film application can cause uneven DFT.

factor_modifiers.name: Sun Exposure Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Sun exposure affects scheduling and daily productive hours. Full sun on aluminum is less critical than vinyl but still affects flash-drying of self-etching primer.
factor_modifiers.notes: Full sun forces early morning scheduling on south/west facades, reducing daily productive hours by ~15%. Self-etching primer is especially sensitive to flash-drying in full sun.

factor_modifiers.name: Surface Temperature Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Surface temperature extends recoat intervals and affects primer cure. Aluminum conducts heat — surface temperature changes faster than vinyl or wood.
factor_modifiers.notes: Cold (<50 deg F surface): slow cure of self-etching primer acid reaction = 30% more time. Hot (>90 deg F surface): flash drying risk = 20% more time.

quality_effects.notes: Economy aluminum repaint. Self-etching primer (mandatory, DFT-critical) + single finish coat. No J-channel detail. No caulk assessment. DFT verification on primer is still required at all tiers — structural bond requirement.

Standard residential aluminum repaint. Self-etching primer + two finish coats. J-channel brush detail. Caulk assessment at siding-to-trim joints. DFT verification for primer. 7-15 year expected service life.

round_configurations.description: Self-etching prime (1 coat, 0.5-1.0 mil) + 1 finish coat — economy aluminum repaint
round_configurations.notes: Minimum viable aluminum repaint. Self-etching primer is mandatory. Single finish coat. Total: 2 coating passes. Prime coat gets higher labor share (DFT control is critical).

round_configurations.description: Self-etching prime (1 coat, 0.5-1.0 mil) + 2 finish coats — standard aluminum repaint
round_configurations.notes: Standard residential repaint. Self-etching primer + two finish coats. J-channel detail included separately. Total: 3 coating passes + detail.

round_configurations.description: Self-etching prime (1 coat) + epoxy intermediate (1 coat) + 1 finish coat — coastal economy
round_configurations.notes: Coastal variant adds epoxy intermediate. Three-layer corrosion barrier. Total: 3 coating passes.

round_configurations.description: Self-etching prime (1 coat) + epoxy intermediate (1 coat) + 2 finish coats — coastal standard
round_configurations.notes: Coastal variant with full coat system. Four coating layers for maximum corrosion protection. Total: 4 coating passes + detail.

assumptions: Base rates are for lap_horizontal aluminum siding at ground access on sound substrate (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT) with chalk_severity=none.
Wash tasks are now separate per chalk_severity (WASH_PRESSURE for none, WASH_CHALK_LIGHT for light, WASH_CHALK_HEAVY for heavy). Chalk modifier on wash is baked into the separate task rates.
Chalk severity modifier (FAC_ALRP_CHALK) applies to oxide scuff and dust cleanup tasks. It does NOT inflate coating application rates.
QT modifier (FAC_ALRP_QT) applies to COATING TASKS ONLY. Prep variation is handled by chalk severity.
Maximum prep modifier stack: heavy chalk (1.75) x scaffold (1.60) = 2.80x. Well under 4.0x cap.
Maximum coating modifier stack: QT3 (1.00) x scaffold (1.60) x full_sun (1.15) x cold_temp (1.30) = 2.39x. Well under 4.0x cap.
Spray is primary application method. No backbrushing on aluminum (non-porous metal). Spray/backbrush coupling rule does NOT apply.
Environmental modifiers (wind, sun, temp) apply only to coating tasks.
Self-etching primer is ALWAYS required — no skip-prime option.
DFT verification for self-etching primer is a mandatory gate at ALL quality tiers.
Epoxy intermediate coat is CONDITIONAL on coastal environment only.
No LRV restriction — any color permitted. No LRV verification gate.
No warranty void gate. No RRP gate.
Substrate state (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT vs SS_EXT_CHALKING) drives chalk_severity assessment but does not change primer chemistry.
Crew size = 1 for all tasks except scaffold setup/teardown (crew size 2).
SOP splits detail work into two tasks: TSK_ALRP_DETAIL_JCHANNEL (SF-based, channel recesses) and TSK_ALRP_DETAIL_CUTIN (LF-based, trim transitions).
SOP consolidates hardscape protection into single task (TSK_ALRP_PROTECT_HARDSCAPE) covering walks, patios, and driveways.
SOP consolidates equipment cleanup into single task (TSK_ALRP_CLEAN_EQUIPMENT) for both spray and brush/roll.
Mobilize and scaffold setup/teardown tasks are new in SOP — fixed-time tasks not present in v0.1.0.
Wash mix task is new in SOP — fixed 10 min for solution preparation.
risks: Cohesive primer failure from over-application of self-etching primer (>1.0 mil DFT). Mitigated by DFT verification gate task, fine-atomization tips, single-pass technique.
Chalk-induced peeling from residual chalk not fully removed. Mitigated by mandatory chalk verification gate and separate wash tasks by chalk severity.
Wrong primer substitution — using standard primer, bonding primer, or STIX adhesion primer instead of self-etching primer. Mitigated by locked material specification and QC verification at delivery.
Oxide reformation between scuff and prime if scheduling delay occurs. Mitigated by SOP same-day sequencing requirement.
Ferrous contamination from steel wool use during oxide scuff. Mitigated by synthetic-only pad specification.
Coastal corrosion without epoxy intermediate layer if environment not assessed correctly. Mitigated by site assessment protocol.
Multi-story projects with scaffold access increase costs by 60%. Ensure access assessment is completed before scope commitment.
Self-etching primer flash-drying in full sun on aluminum. Mitigated by sun exposure modifier and early-morning scheduling.

validation_plan.test: Self-etching primer spray production rate — 400-450 SF/hr claimed vs field actual
validation_plan.method: Time spray of self-etching primer with fine-atomization tips on aluminum siding at ground level. Record SF completed per hour AND DFT achieved.
validation_plan.acceptance: Within 350-500 SF/hr range AND DFT within 0.5-1.0 mil

validation_plan.test: Oxide scuff rate — 250 SF/hr claimed vs field actual
validation_plan.method: Time oxide scuff with synthetic abrasive pads on aluminum siding at ground level. Record SF completed per hour and pad consumption rate.

validation_plan.test: Finish spray rate on primed aluminum — 400-500 SF/hr
validation_plan.method: Time acrylic finish spray on primed aluminum siding. Note coverage rate (SF/gal) alongside production rate.

validation_plan.test: Pressure wash rate by chalk severity
validation_plan.method: Time pressure wash on aluminum siding at various chalk severity levels. Record effective rate per severity.
Time brush detail work at J-channels and under-sill channels on QT3 aluminum project.
Time brush cut-in at trim transitions on QT3 aluminum project.

validation_plan.test: Access modifier calibration — ladder 1.35x on aluminum
validation_plan.method: Compare timed spray at ground vs ladder on same surface. Calculate actual ratio.

validation_plan.test: DFT verification task time — 15 min per zone
validation_plan.method: Time DFT gauge spot-check procedure on 3-5 elevation sections. Record actual minutes per zone.
